CHIEF COMPLAINT
Runny nose, nasal congestion, and cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 5-year-old male presenting with symptoms that started around supper time last night. Parent reports runny nose with clear mucous and nasal congestion. Patient has a cough that is not barky. Parent notes patient has been pulling on his ears and rubbing at his nose. Rectal temperature was 100.3°F. Appetite has been variable - ate well last night, consumed about 7 ounces from bottle this morning, barely finished a second bottle, and refused cereal. Patient is energetic but irritable and fighting sleep. Older sister has been sick. Patient also had recent play date with nephew who had a sinus infection. Home remedies attempted include saline mist to nose, Tylenol given early this morning, baby Vick's on feet last night, and humidifier use. Additionally, cradle cap has worsened; parent using cradle cap brush and regular Aveeno shampoo.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Runny nose with clear mucous, nasal congestion, cough (non-barky), ear pulling, nasal rubbing, low-grade fever (100.3°F rectal), decreased appetite, irritability, insomnia, and worsened cradle cap.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol, saline mist, baby Vick's, humidifier.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sister currently sick with similar symptoms.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recent play date with nephew who had sinus infection.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Ears: Appear normal. Exam otherwise unremarkable.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Viral upper respiratory infection, likely starting as viral with potential for bacterial progression. Cradle cap (seborrheic dermatitis). Plan: Continue fluids and rest. Monitor closely for barking cough development. Prescribed sister's cough medicine (half teaspoon dose) to have on hand in case barky cough develops; only use if barky cough develops, for 5 days if needed. Recommend Zarbee's cough syrup for regular cough using under-one-year-old dose. For cradle cap, use dandruff shampoo (Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD regular strength) twice weekly, continue soft brush with baby oil to remove scales, avoid eyes during rinsing. No antibiotics at this time. Follow-up appointment in one week. Patient to return sooner if condition worsens.
